note: One row per reference module and per gap-register item, each with a status and at least one path that must exist. `python/tests/test_parity_register.py` fails when a path disappears, when an item loses its status, or when a deferred item has no recorded decision. Statuses: ported = the mechanism was transcribed; equivalent = Eclipse already had it under a different shape; not_applicable = the product shape differs; deferred = a written decision to not do it. `tests` + `testSymbol` are the behaviour half: each claim about a mechanism must name a test file that contains that symbol, so a row cannot pass on file presence alone. `behaviour` is the numeric half: a row may cite tests that assert the reference's own values on a shared fixture, which is what separates 'we have a module with that name' from 'our module computes what theirs computes'. Behavioural comparisons that found a difference are recorded in the row's `note`: a register that only ever says 'equivalent' is not being read carefully. Two more rows got numeric comparisons after the first four: research_artifacts (evidence multiset diff) and br_data (B3 cash/odd-lot symbol mapping). Eight rows now carry a behaviour comparison; the rest remain on file/test/symbol and are named as such. Thirty-two rows now carry a behaviour comparison — PARITY COMPLETE (scheduled_research is now wired, not library-only); the rest remain on file/test/symbol and are named as such.

modules.note: The tool surface was equivalent, but there was NO guard against a shell command that kills every Python process by name — `pkill python`, `taskkill /IM python.exe`, `powershell Stop-Process -Name python`. That kills the HARNESS mid-run: the command looks successful and then the agent's own process is gone. Ported the reference's check (per shell segment so `&& pkill python` is caught, quotes flattened, case-insensitive, actionable refusal) and wired it into code/shell.py BEFORE the sandbox spawns, so the refusal costs nothing and the harness stays alive. One shared limit is stated: a bare `get-process python | stop-process` without a powershell prefix is not matched, in either codebase.

behaviour.checks: fifteen broad Python-kill spellings refused (pkill/killall/sudo, taskkill /IM, PowerShell Stop-Process by name and by pipe, hidden after && or ; or a newline, any case) and twelve targeted or unrelated commands allowed, including `kill -9 <pid>`, `pkill -f uvicorn` and a quoted mention
